cues.text: Welcome to SuiFleet. Click Connect Wallet and choose Slush, an extension, or Google where available.
This recording uses a scripted test wallet in place of Slush; approve the connection.
Connected: the card shows your address and the network (Testnet).
First time only: create your default fleet, then approve the transaction.
Your fleet is selected in the Fleet switcher. Next: fund its network budget.
Choose Network budget in the sidebar.
Enter a deposit in Sui. Devices draw report and storage fees from this budget, within your limits.
Approve the deposit in your wallet. A budget is created only if your fleet needs one.
Confirmed. The balance under Keep devices reporting now covers device activity.
Choose Devices in the sidebar.
Click Register by address. The address comes from the device: the client’s derive-address command.
Click Register and approve the transaction.
Your device is registered. Health reports begin when its client starts.
For a production batch, choose Enrollment in the sidebar.
First, create a batch policy: how many devices may enroll, and for how long.
Next, reserve names and serial numbers: paste a roster CSV and click Check.
Download the credentials: the only copy of the claim keys, for your factory provisioning media.
Then register the claims in your fleet. Each device then enrolls itself at first boot.
Choose Components in the sidebar to publish software.
First time only: set up your publisher catalog and approve the transaction.
Name the component and give the release a semantic version.
Choose the platform and attach the artifact for it.
Delivery: choose Confidential for proprietary software. This public demo artifact is published unencrypted.
Review, then upload to Walrus and register the version. Approve the transaction.
Version published. It is now in the library, ready to deploy.
On Devices, open the Device groups tab and create a group.
Click Manage and add the device to the group.
In the component library, choose Deploy this version.
Select the group as the target. This catalog release creates a one-shot deployment.
Click Deploy and approve. Each device in the group checks its membership and applies it.
Deployment created. Devices report signed results under Deployments.
Choose Rollouts in the sidebar to release in stages.
Open Create a gradual rollout and fill in the version, recipe and digests.
List the cohorts, one line each; the first cohort goes first.
Set the pacing, bake period and abort threshold, then create the rollout.
Select the rollout, then admit the first devices after checking device health.
The rollout advances only on healthy signed reports. Pause or abort at any time.
Open Access policies. A policy controls decryption for confidential releases.
Choose Group and select guide-pilot. Membership determines which devices may request keys.
Revoking access stops future requests. It cannot recall software already decrypted.
Open Fleet settings to choose reporting and update intervals.
Review the estimate, then save. Saving settings does not add money to the budget.
This small demo budget does not cover the estimate. Save anyway records settings only; it adds no funds.
Devices apply settings at their next check. Network budget holds their funds separately.

voice_description: Female, American English; synthetic Kokoro Heart voice
note: Cue times refer to the original cursor recordings. Narration retimes each segment without dropping actions or speeding up speech. Synthetic voice, not a recording of a human presenter.
